chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, who said:
Jibrāʾīl descended upon Ādam عليه السلام and said: “O Ādam, I have been commanded to give you a choice of one out of three, so choose one and leave two.”
He said to him: “And what are those three?” He said: “Intellect, modesty, and religion.” Ādam عليه السلام said: “Then I have chosen intellect.”

Then Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام said to modesty and religion: “Depart and leave him.” So they both said: “O Jibrāʾīl, we have been commanded to be with intellect wherever it may be.” He said: “Then that is your affair,” and he ascended.

key_terms.أُمِرْنَا: we were commanded; indicating divine instruction
key_terms.الدِّينُ: religion; the divinely ordained way of belief and conduct
key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: modesty or moral shame that restrains a person from wrongdoing
key_terms.الْعَقْلُ: intellect; the faculty of sound reason and discernment
key_terms.هَبَطَ جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl descended; marking a revelatory encounter

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the relationship between intellect, modesty, and religion?
ai.summary: This hadith presents intellect as the central gift with which modesty and religion remain inseparably joined. It highlights, in concise symbolic form, that true religion and moral shame are grounded in sound reason and accompany it wherever it is found.
